positive: This invention pertains to combinations used for agricultural enhancements, specifically focusing on mixtures that leverage active thiocarbamate with synergistic elements to bolster its performance. The pairing of thiocarbamate with certain inert compounds leads to an augmentation in the longevity of the herbicidal action of thiocarbamate when applied to farmlands. Thiocarbamate, a compound acknowledged for its weed combating properties in various crops, displays amplified retention in soil composition when merged with selected enhancers devoid of inherent herbicidal properties. Experimental evidence suggests a tangible improvement in the duration of thiocarbamate's potency, confirmed through agricultural assays measuring weed suppression over extended periods. A new class of inert enhancer compounds is disclosed, demonstrating through soil analysis the capability to mitigate the degradation rate of thiocarbamate in the soil, thus preserving its plant growth inhibitory function. The invention discloses a unique herbicidal formulation including an effective portion of a thiocarbamate and a specific quantity of an inert synergistic compound, with optimal ratios disclosed for maximizing the duration of herbicidal impact in soil environments. Illustrations of appropriate thiocarbamates and enhancer compounds are provided, showing a coherent approach to boosting thiocarbamate performance without adverse ecological impacts. The disclosed methods capitalize on the synergistic relationship between the active and inert components, providing an innovative solution to maintaining prolonged herbicidal action.
negative: The invention outlines a sophisticated container system designated for handling various substances that require segregation while maintaining a sterile enclosure. The design focuses on a separation process that leverages a first chamber for containing the substance and a second chamber dedicated to holding a solvent or reagent. An external force is applied to both chambers simultaneously, enabling the expulsion of the substance from the first chamber and the solvent from the second one. The expelled mixture then travels through a conduit system with branches that allow for the mixing of the substance with the solvent. Followed by the conduit, a separation unit, which does not necessarily utilize filtration, is tasked with cleansing the substance from any undesired elements. In the preferred application of this design, the separation unit efficiently removes specific impurities that hinder the purity of the substance without necessitating the invasive introduction of external elements, keeping the system intact and sterile throughout the operation. While the described method is notably applicable to a variety of substances, it has particular advantages for processing materials sensitive to contamination and requiring aseptic conditions.

anchor: FIELD OF INVENTION [0001] The invention relates generally to cardiac rhythm management, and more particularly to a combination of cardiac pacing and optimizing pacing parameter values. DISCUSSION OF PRIOR ART [0002] Dual-Chamber Pacemakers [0003] Dual-Chamber pacemakers are used increasingly in patients with varying degrees of heart block, symptomatic bradydysrhythmias, and drug-refractory cardiomyopathy. Clinical benefits of the dual-chamber pacemaker include enhancement of forward blood flow, a feature that can alleviate symptoms of congestive heart failure (CHF), and prevention of atrial fibrillation caused by the atria contracting against a closed valve (Gadler F, Linde C, Darpo B. Modification of atrioventricular conduction as adjunct therapy for pacemaker-treated patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy. Eur Heart J 1998; 19:132-138). [0004] Dual-chamber pacing can improve hemodynamics in some patients with dilated cardiomyopathy, likely by abolishing diastolic mitral regurgitation through the establishment of mechanical atrial and ventricular synchrony (Nishimura R, Hayes D, Holmes D, Tajik A. Mechanism of hemodynamic improvement by dual-chamber pacing for severe left ventricular dysfunction: An acute Doppler and catheterization hemodynamic study. J Am Coil Cardiol 1995; 25:281-288). Despite the benefit of optimization of atrioventricular (AV) delay, dual-chamber pacemakers often are left at the default value, which the manufacturer sets to approximately 170 milliseconds (Kindermann M, Frohlig G, Doerr T, Schieffer H. Optimizing the AV delay in DDD pacemakers with high degree AVE block: Mitral valve Doppler versus impedance cardiography. Pacing Clin Electrophysiol 1997; 20: 2453-2462). It is the consensus of independent researchers that optimization of AV interval is not routinely performed. Procedures for pacemaker optimization, specifically obtaining stroke volume measurements at different AV intervals by aortic Doppler echocardiography , traditionally have been observer-dependent, time-consuming, and costly. [0005] The goal of AV optimization is the synchronization of the completion of end-diastolic filling exactly at the onset of left ventricular contraction. Obviously, to accomplish this objective, precise physiological measurements of the events of the cardiac cycle must be obtained. Because of a wide range of cardiac conditions, status of the ventricles, and cardioactive medications, each and every patient is unique. Leonelli et al. (Leonelli F, Wang K, Youssef M, Brown D. Systolic and diastolic effects of variable atrioventricular delay in patients with pacemakers. Eur Heart J 1995; 15:1431-1440) observed that an optimal setting of the AV delay value improved stroke volume up to 42%. [0006] Another application of cardiac pacemakers has recently been discovered: Recent reports are suggesting that biventricular pacing may offer some important options in the treatment of patients with congestive heart failure (CHF). A significant percentage of patients with CHF have conduction abnormalities on EGG. These conduction abnormalities result in abnormal activation of ventricular myocardium and asynchronous activation of the atrial and ventricular chambers. Biventricular pacing attempts to activate the right and left ventricles simultaneously, producing what is termed “ventricular resynchronization”. [0007] Studies have confirmed acute and short-term hemodynamic benefits of biventricular pacing. In addition, studies have documented improvement in the functional status of patients with CHF. Larger, prospective studies investigating the beneficial effects of biventricular pacing and its clinical implications are currently underway. [0008] In addition to the symptomatic and functional improvements, other important changes have been noted in CHF patients treated with biventricular pacing. Parameters of cardiac function such as left ventricular dimensions and myocardial performance index have improved markedly. Elevated plasma norepinephrine levels, which are associated with increased mortality in CHF, improve in biventricular pacing. Decreased heart rate variability, also associated with increased risk of sudden death in CHF, has been shown to improve. These findings have lead investigators to hypothesize the potential for biventricular pacing to improve survival. This being said, no trial to date has demonstrated a survival benefit to biventricular pacing. Furthermore, no studies are known that investigate the effects, and potential benefits, of biventricular pacing forcing a small delay between right ventricular and left ventricular contraction, or vice versa. [0009] Optimization Techniques [0010] When optimizing the AV delay, or any other delay such as a delay between the contraction of right and left ventricles, it must be tailored to the individual patient. For almost two decades, stroke volume measurements by means of thoracic electrical bioimpedance (TEB) have been favorably considered for optimal determination of pacemaker settings. More recently, Hayes et al. (Hayes D, Hayes S, Hyberger L. Atrioventricular interval optimization technique: Impedance measurements vs Echo/Doppler. Presented at the North American Society for Pacing & Electrophysiology's 19th Annual Scientific Sessions, San Diego, Calif., May 9, 1998) reported that the noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring with TEB permits determination of optimal AV delay within 15 minutes in any clinical settings. [0011] Despite promising benefits to the patient, the utilization of thoracic electrical bioimpedance (TEB), as with any other aforementioned method, has not been established as a standard optimization procedure for the setting of parameter values of dual-chamber pacemakers. Apparently, the TEB procedure, applied during pacemaker follow-up, is time-consuming and requires active involvement of the physician during the entire optimization period. [0012] Rate-responsive cardiac pacemakers address the adaptation of the pacing rate according to the physiological demands related to the activity of the pacemaker patient. Sensors determine, for example, posture and movement of the patient, or respiration, characterized by respiration rate and tidal volume, and even stroke volume by measurement of thoracic electrical bioimpedance. The pacemaker adapts the pacing rate depending on the information obtained by the sensors and processed usually by the pacemaker. The pacemaker's rate adapted to the patient's activity is not within the scope of the aforementioned optimization techniques, and the invention. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [0013] The new method and apparatus defined in the appended claims incorporate a cardiac pacemaker and thoracic electrical bioimpedance (TEB) measuring approach. With this combination of a diagnostic (TEB) and therapeutic method and apparatus (pacemaker) a closed-loop system is created to obtain, within its confines, an optimal setting of pacing parameter values. [0014] In a preferred embodiment, a specific optimization cycle, triggered by an operator or upon the expiration of a preset time interval, automatically permutates the values of one or more pacing parameters, such as AV delays, inter-atrial delay, inter-ventricular delay, or heart rate, within operator-defined ranges, and determines at each permutation of parameter values hemodynamic parameters, such as stroke volume (SV), cardiac output (CO), ejection fraction (EF), and other indices of ventricular performance. [0015] The operator defines one or more pacing parameters, such as atrioventricular delays, inter-atrial delay, inter-ventricular delay, or heart rate, which are subject to variation during an optimization cycle. Furthermore, the operator defines a variation range for values of each pacing parameter and a variation step width for stepping through the variation range during the optimization cycle. The number of pacing parameters subject to variation and the number of applicable variation steps for each parameter determine the number of permutations of pacing parameter values and, thus, the sequence of the optimization cycle. Each permutation of pacing parameter values is applied, for example, for a pre-defined period in the range of 30 to 120 seconds. The pacing parameter value, which results in the maximum value of a hemodynamic parameter, or a combination thereof, is the output of the optimization cycle and adapted by the cardiac pacemaker for further stimulation. [0016] The hemodynamic measurements are performed utilizing the apparatus and method of Bernstein and Osypka as described in detail in European patent application No. 02007310.2 of the present applicant, Osypka Medical GmbH, Berlin, for APPARATUS AND METHOD FOR DETERMINING AN APPROXIMATE VALUE OF THE STROKE VOLUME AND THE CARDIAC OUTPUT OF THE HEART, filed concurrently herewith (in the following referred to as the Osypka EP application No. 02007310.2), the disclosure of which is incorporated herein by reference. [0017] The optimization cycle automatically executed for a number of permutations of pacing parameter values to obtain maximal left-ventricular function enhances significantly the time-efficacy of an otherwise cumbersome and time-consuming, but nevertheless beneficial method. This automatic optimization method can be applied during pacing system analysis (PSA) prior to permanent pacemaker implantation, during temporary pacing following cardiothoracic surgery, during follow-up of a patient with an implantable pacemaker, or during the investigation of efficacy of pacing algorithms for patients undergoing treatment for congestive heart failure (CHF). [0029] The processing unit 110 of the optimization apparatus 100 processes the permutations of the pacing parameter values, such as heart rate, and atrioventricular (AV), inter-atrial (AA) and inter-ventricular (VV) delays, and records the corresponding measurements of stroke volume, cardiac output, ejection fraction (EF) and other indices of ventricular performance. [0030] According to the invention, a specific optimization cycle, triggered by an operator or upon the expiration of a preset time interval, automatically varies one or more pacing parameters, such as AV delays, inter-atrial delay, inter-ventricular delay, or heart rate, within operator-defined ranges, and determines at each parameter setting hemodynamic parameters, such as stroke volume (SV), cardiac output (GO), and other indices of ventricular performance. positive: FIELD OF INVENTION [0001] The innovation pertains specifically to advancements in neurostimulation for managing chronic pain. Focus is directed towards an apparatus that combines neural sensing and stimulating capabilities with optimal parameter selection. DISCUSSION OF PRIOR ART [0002] Spinal Cord Stimulators [0003] Spinal cord stimulators are increasingly utilized to manage various forms of chronic pain, included but not limited to neuropathic pain, failed back surgery syndrome, and complex regional pain syndrome. Patient-reported outcomes signal improvements in pain thresholds and overall quality of life, much like the benefits seen in cardiac rhythm management for enhancing blood flow. [0004] The process of selecting optimal parameters for neurostimulation, including pulse width, amplitude, and frequency, is often left to default values due to lack of individualization. However, the clinical consensus suggests a need for routine optimization tailored to each patient's pain profile. Techniques for optimization of stimulation parameters are often described as time-consuming and resource-intensive, similarly to cardiac pacing parameter optimization. [0005] One aim of optimization in neural pacing is to target the most effective frequencies to disrupt pain signals without causing discomfort or muscular contractions. This requires precise physiological measurements and an understanding that each patient may respond differently to stimulation based on their unique nervous system pathology. [0006] With the concept of neuroplasticity, recent innovations in the field have considered the benefits of adaptive stimulation patterns that respond to the dynamic nature of chronic pain. Despite some studies indicating immediate relief during initial trials, long-term benefits and functional status improvements require further investigation. [0007] Without significant trial evidence, there is no conclusive data that adaptive neural pacing parameters lead to a decided improvement in patient survival rates or a decrease in the use of pain medication. The potential for varying stimulation onset or creating minor delays in the patterning of pulses has not been thoroughly evaluated. [0008] Stimulation Optimization Techniques [0010] Customizing neural stimulation parameters requires consideration of patient-specific neural activity and pain patterns. Although studies pertaining to thoracic electrical bioimpedance have been discussed in the cardiac domain, its application in neural stimulation parameter optimization remains unexplored. [0011] Despite the promise of alleviating chronic pain, the usage and standardization of optimization procedures in the context of neural stimulators is not widely adopted. The procedure, when conducted, can be lengthy and necessitates the involvement of a skilled clinician throughout the period of optimization. [0012] Adaptable neural stimulators are being explored to accommodate changes in patient's posture or levels of activity, identified by sensing axial movements or analyzing neural signals. Nevertheless, these advanced features lie outside the scope of customary optimization routines and the innovation at hand. SUMMARY OF THE INNOVATION [0013] The current proposal outlines a combined neural sensing and stimulation device that also incorporates a system for optimizing stimulation parameters. [0014] A preferred embodiment includes a cycle where stimulation values, such as pulse width and frequency, are automatically varied based on pre-set schedules or upon operator invocation. Measurement of pain thresholds at each variation is recorded to identify optimal settings that provide the most relief. [0015] The clinician can define neural stimulation parameters to vary during the optimization cycle. Additionally, ranges for each parameter's values and the step width for variations can be set. An extensive number of permutations of these parameters will lead to the identification of the most suitable setting for pain management. [0016] Hemodynamic measurements, commonly seen in cardiac applications, are substituted here by neural response indicators. These can include, but are not limited to, patient-reported outcomes and physiological assessments of pain response. [0017] An advanced cycle automatically executed for numerous permutations of stimulation parameters measures thresholds to obtain maximal pain relief, significantly enhancing efficiency over traditional methods. This system can be employed during neural stimulator analysis pre- or post-implantation or during clinical evaluations of new pain management protocols. BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS [0019] FIG. 1 illustrates an embodiment where the optimization device and neural stimulator are integrated into one unit. [0020] FIG. 2 illustrates an embodiment where the optimization device and neural stimulator function as separate units. [0021] FIG. 3 illustrates the steps of the automatic optimization process. [0022] FIG. 4 describes the sensing and stimulation sequence of the applied neural modulation techniques. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS [0024] FIG. 1 details an apparatus applied in pain management protocols, involving an external or implantable neural stimulator. [0025] The patient interface integrates sensors to monitor neural activity and therapeutic electrodes for delivering targeted stimulation. The optimization apparatus is directly linked with the stimulator, allowing for seamless parameter adjustment based on real-time feedback. [0026] Clinical trials indicate that the method provides discernible improvement in pain management, with enhancements to functionality and patient autonomy. [0027] The apparatus may also be used in conjunction with pharmacologic interventions, providing a multifaceted approach to chronic pain management. [0028] Adaptations for individual patient needs and the dynamic nature of chronic pain are essential features of this new pain management paradigm. [0029] FIG. 2 displays an alternative setup, where the neural stimulator and optimization device function independently but share data to achieve optimal settings. [0030] Further details indicate the potential for integration with mobile applications, facilitating remote monitoring and adjustment of the stimulator settings. [0031] The extended descriptions affirm the innovative nature of merging neural sensing with actionable stimulation strategies, leading to optimal outcomes in the management of chronic pain.
negative: FIELD OF INVENTION [0001] The invention pertains to advancements in vehicular power systems, in particular to a method that harmonizes power distribution with engine performance optimization. DISCUSSION OF PRIOR ART [0002] Hybrid Power Systems [0003] Hybrid power systems in vehicles have gained prominence for their ability to improve fuel efficiency and reduce emissions. The benefits of these systems include the maximization of fuel utilization, reduction of greenhouse gases, and the provision of an auxiliary power source during engine off-cycles. However, despite the benefits of efficient power management, hybrid systems often operate on predetermined protocols which may not be optimal for every driving condition. Advanced sensors can enhance the efficiency of such systems, yet no widespread standard for sensor-driven power optimization exists. [0004] Harmonizing power flow in conjunction with sensor inputs can yield significant efficiency improvements in some vehicles with a hybrid power train, by addressing power distribution during various engine phases. Despite the potential of sensor-based optimization of power control mechanisms, such systems are commonly calibrated to OEM specifications, which might not always align with real-world driving scenarios. Current research does highlight the need for adaptive power management systems but fails to establish a universally accepted methodology. [0006] Another area of interest within the automotive industry is the development of all-electric vehicles (EVs) that utilize battery packs for propulsion. The management of battery performance and longevity is a critical aspect of EV operation. Although attempts have been made to integrate advanced battery management systems, the efficacy of such strategies in real-world conditions has yet to be affirmed through comprehensive studies. [0009] Optimization Techniques [0010] When optimizing power distribution or engine performance parameters, the approach needs to be tailored to the specific vehicle and its usage patterns. For years, real-time vehicle data monitoring has been suggested as a potential solution, yet implementing such systems has proven to be complex. Techniques such as utilizing vehicle telematics for predictive maintenance and adaptive control strategies are promising, yet their adoption across the industry remains sporadic. [0011] Despite the promise shown by these advanced systems, their application as a standard procedure for optimizing hybrid or electric vehicle performance has not been established. The complexity and the need for constant calibration based on sensor feedback have made their widespread utilization challenging. [0012] Rate-responsive automotive systems have been introduced to address the dynamic needs of power distribution based on driving conditions. Such systems use a variety of sensors to detect, for example, acceleration, vehicle inclination, or driving patterns, adjusting the power distribution as necessary. While these innovations mark progress in the field, they fall outside the scope of conventional power system optimization, distinctly separate from the topic at hand. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [0013] The novel method and apparatus outlined herein detail an integrated vehicle power system that combines sensor input with advanced algorithms to create a closed-loop system for optimal engine performance. [0014] In a preferred embodiment, the system automatically assesses various power system parameters, such as battery charge state, alternator output, and energy recovery efficiency, and adjusts these parameters as necessary to maximize vehicle performance. [0015] The defined optimization process, initiated either by an operator or automatically at set intervals, systematically tests and records data pertaining to various powertrain parameters. [0016] Vehicle performance measurements are performed utilizing advanced diagnostics as detailed in a concurrent automotive patent application by the applicant. [0017] Through an automatic and systematic approach, the novel method significantly streamlines the optimization process, making it less cumbersome and more time-efficient than traditional techniques. [0018] Other advantages, features, and objectives of the invention will become apparent from the following descriptions. DISCUSSION OF PRIOR ART [0002] Dual-Chamber Pacemakers [0003] Dual-Chamber pacemakers are used increasingly in patients with varying degrees of heart block, symptomatic bradydysrhythmias, and drug-refractory cardiomyopathy. Clinical benefits of the dual-chamber pacemaker include enhancement of forward blood flow, a feature that can alleviate symptoms of congestive heart failure (CHF), and prevention of atrial fibrillation caused by the atria contracting against a closed valve (Gadler F, Linde C, Darpo B. Modification of atrioventricular conduction as adjunct therapy for pacemaker-treated patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy. Eur Heart J 1998; 19:132-138). [0004] Dual-chamber pacing can improve hemodynamics in some patients with dilated cardiomyopathy, likely by abolishing diastolic mitral regurgitation through the establishment of mechanical atrial and ventricular synchrony (Nishimura R, Hayes D, Holmes D, Tajik A. Mechanism of hemodynamic improvement by dual-chamber pacing for severe left ventricular dysfunction: An acute Doppler and catheterization hemodynamic study. J Am Coil Cardiol 1995; 25:281-288). Despite the benefit of optimization of atrioventricular (AV) delay, dual-chamber pacemakers often are left at the default value, which the manufacturer sets to approximately 170 milliseconds (Kindermann M, Frohlig G, Doerr T, Schieffer H. Optimizing the AV delay in DDD pacemakers with high degree AVE block: Mitral valve Doppler versus impedance cardiography. Pacing Clin Electrophysiol 1997; 20: 2453-2462). It is the consensus of independent researchers that optimization of AV interval is not routinely performed. Procedures for pacemaker optimization, specifically obtaining stroke volume measurements at different AV intervals by aortic Doppler echocardiography , traditionally have been observer-dependent, time-consuming, and costly. [0005] The goal of AV optimization is the synchronization of the completion of end-diastolic filling exactly at the onset of left ventricular contraction. Obviously, to accomplish this objective, precise physiological measurements of the events of the cardiac cycle must be obtained. Because of a wide range of cardiac conditions, status of the ventricles, and cardioactive medications, each and every patient is unique. Leonelli et al. (Leonelli F, Wang K, Youssef M, Brown D. Systolic and diastolic effects of variable atrioventricular delay in patients with pacemakers. Eur Heart J 1995; 15:1431-1440) observed that an optimal setting of the AV delay value improved stroke volume up to 42%. [0006] Another application of cardiac pacemakers has recently been discovered: Recent reports are suggesting that biventricular pacing may offer some important options in the treatment of patients with congestive heart failure (CHF). A significant percentage of patients with CHF have conduction abnormalities on EGG. These conduction abnormalities result in abnormal activation of ventricular myocardium and asynchronous activation of the atrial and ventricular chambers. Biventricular pacing attempts to activate the right and left ventricles simultaneously, producing what is termed “ventricular resynchronization”. [0007] Studies have confirmed acute and short-term hemodynamic benefits of biventricular pacing. In addition, studies have documented improvement in the functional status of patients with CHF. Larger, prospective studies investigating the beneficial effects of biventricular pacing and its clinical implications are currently underway. [0008] In addition to the symptomatic and functional improvements, other important changes have been noted in CHF patients treated with biventricular pacing. Parameters of cardiac function such as left ventricular dimensions and myocardial performance index have improved markedly. Elevated plasma norepinephrine levels, which are associated with increased mortality in CHF, improve in biventricular pacing. Decreased heart rate variability, also associated with increased risk of sudden death in CHF, has been shown to improve. These findings have lead investigators to hypothesize the potential for biventricular pacing to improve survival. This being said, no trial to date has demonstrated a survival benefit to biventricular pacing. Furthermore, no studies are known that investigate the effects, and potential benefits, of biventricular pacing forcing a small delay between right ventricular and left ventricular contraction, or vice versa. [0009] Optimization Techniques [0010] When optimizing the AV delay, or any other delay such as a delay between the contraction of right and left ventricles, it must be tailored to the individual patient. For almost two decades, stroke volume measurements by means of thoracic electrical bioimpedance (TEB) have been favorably considered for optimal determination of pacemaker settings. More recently, Hayes et al. (Hayes D, Hayes S, Hyberger L. Atrioventricular interval optimization technique: Impedance measurements vs Echo/Doppler. Presented at the North American Society for Pacing & Electrophysiology's 19th Annual Scientific Sessions, San Diego, Calif., May 9, 1998) reported that the noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring with TEB permits determination of optimal AV delay within 15 minutes in any clinical settings. Apparently, the TEB procedure, applied during pacemaker follow-up, is time-consuming and requires active involvement of the physician during the entire optimization period. [0012] Rate-responsive cardiac pacemakers address the adaptation of the pacing rate according to the physiological demands related to the activity of the pacemaker patient. Sensors determine, for example, posture and movement of the patient, or respiration, characterized by respiration rate and tidal volume, and even stroke volume by measurement of thoracic electrical bioimpedance. The pacemaker adapts the pacing rate depending on the information obtained by the sensors and processed usually by the pacemaker. positive: FIELD OF INVENTION [0001] The invention pertains broadly to the management of cardiovascular health, specifically to advancements in electromechanical devices designed to correct cardiac dysrhythmias. BRIEF REVIEW OF RELEVANT TECHNOLOGIES [0002] Single-Chamber Pacemakers [0003] Employed frequently for individuals with various forms of atrioventricular blocks and symptomatic bradyarrhythmias, single-chamber pacemakers have been known to contribute to the improvement of cardiac output by facilitating consistent ventricular contractions. However, the adjustment of device settings, such as pacing intervals, typically remains unchanged from manufacturer presets, contributing to less than optimal therapeutic outcomes. [0004] Although single-chamber device implantations are noted for their simplicity and lower cost compared to more complex systems, their inability to synchronize atrial and ventricular contractions can be disadvantageous for patients needing more precise cardiac cycle management. [0005] The challenge remains to identify a universally effective optimization protocol for personalizing pacing parameters, without incurring prohibitive costs or unduly burdening medical practitioners with complex procedures. Discussions in the field continue regarding the best practices for individualizing treatment to enhance cardiac function and prevent arrhythmogenic complications. [0006] Despite the growing consensus on the need for personalized care, the industry has not yet standardized an approach to modifying pacing parameters in response to patient-specific cardiac conditions. Furthermore, the direct impact of such optimizations on clinical outcomes, particularly in the context of single-chamber pacemakers, remains inadequately explored. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [0013] The proposed method and apparatus do not claim to introduce the use of thoracic electrical bioimpedance (TEB) measurements in conjunction with pacing devices. Instead, the innovation focuses on creating a semi-automated framework aimed at facilitating the adjustment of pacing parameters while considering individual patient characteristics. [0014] The preferred embodiment involves a semi-automated cycle that is initiated by a clinician or after a pre-set duration. However, the clinical consensus suggests a need for routine optimization tailored to each patient's pain profile. Techniques for optimization of stimulation parameters are often described as time-consuming and resource-intensive, similarly to cardiac pacing parameter optimization. [0005] One aim of optimization in neural pacing is to target the most effective frequencies to disrupt pain signals without causing discomfort or muscular contractions. This requires precise physiological measurements and an understanding that each patient may respond differently to stimulation based on their unique nervous system pathology. [0006] With the concept of neuroplasticity, recent innovations in the field have considered the benefits of adaptive stimulation patterns that respond to the dynamic nature of chronic pain. Despite some studies indicating immediate relief during initial trials, long-term benefits and functional status improvements require further investigation. [0007] Without significant trial evidence, there is no conclusive data that adaptive neural pacing parameters lead to a decided improvement in patient survival rates or a decrease in the use of pain medication. The potential for varying stimulation onset or creating minor delays in the patterning of pulses has not been thoroughly evaluated. [0008] Stimulation Optimization Techniques [0010] Customizing neural stimulation parameters requires consideration of patient-specific neural activity and pain patterns. Although studies pertaining to thoracic electrical bioimpedance have been discussed in the cardiac domain, its application in neural stimulation parameter optimization remains unexplored. [0011] Despite the promise of alleviating chronic pain, the usage and standardization of optimization procedures in the context of neural stimulators is not widely adopted. The procedure, when conducted, can be lengthy and necessitates the involvement of a skilled clinician throughout the period of optimization. [0012] Adaptable neural stimulators are being explored to accommodate changes in patient's posture or levels of activity, identified by sensing axial movements or analyzing neural signals. anchor: FIELD OF INVENTION [0001] The invention relates generally to cardiac rhythm management, and more particularly to a combination of cardiac pacing and optimizing pacing parameter values. DISCUSSION OF PRIOR ART [0002] Dual-Chamber Pacemakers [0003] Dual-Chamber pacemakers are used increasingly in patients with varying degrees of heart block, symptomatic bradydysrhythmias, and drug-refractory cardiomyopathy. Clinical benefits of the dual-chamber pacemaker include enhancement of forward blood flow, a feature that can alleviate symptoms of congestive heart failure (CHF), and prevention of atrial fibrillation caused by the atria contracting against a closed valve (Gadler F, Linde C, Darpo B. Modification of atrioventricular conduction as adjunct therapy for pacemaker-treated patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy. Eur Heart J 1998; 19:132-138). [0004] Dual-chamber pacing can improve hemodynamics in some patients with dilated cardiomyopathy, likely by abolishing diastolic mitral regurgitation through the establishment of mechanical atrial and ventricular synchrony (Nishimura R, Hayes D, Holmes D, Tajik A. Mechanism of hemodynamic improvement by dual-chamber pacing for severe left ventricular dysfunction: An acute Doppler and catheterization hemodynamic study. J Am Coil Cardiol 1995; 25:281-288). Despite the benefit of optimization of atrioventricular (AV) delay, dual-chamber pacemakers often are left at the default value, which the manufacturer sets to approximately 170 milliseconds (Kindermann M, Frohlig G, Doerr T, Schieffer H. Optimizing the AV delay in DDD pacemakers with high degree AVE block: Mitral valve Doppler versus impedance cardiography. Pacing Clin Electrophysiol 1997; 20: 2453-2462). It is the consensus of independent researchers that optimization of AV interval is not routinely performed. Procedures for pacemaker optimization, specifically obtaining stroke volume measurements at different AV intervals by aortic Doppler echocardiography , traditionally have been observer-dependent, time-consuming, and costly. [0005] The goal of AV optimization is the synchronization of the completion of end-diastolic filling exactly at the onset of left ventricular contraction. Obviously, to accomplish this objective, precise physiological measurements of the events of the cardiac cycle must be obtained. Because of a wide range of cardiac conditions, status of the ventricles, and cardioactive medications, each and every patient is unique. Leonelli et al. (Leonelli F, Wang K, Youssef M, Brown D. Systolic and diastolic effects of variable atrioventricular delay in patients with pacemakers. Eur Heart J 1995; 15:1431-1440) observed that an optimal setting of the AV delay value improved stroke volume up to 42%. [0006] Another application of cardiac pacemakers has recently been discovered: Recent reports are suggesting that biventricular pacing may offer some important options in the treatment of patients with congestive heart failure (CHF). A significant percentage of patients with CHF have conduction abnormalities on EGG. These conduction abnormalities result in abnormal activation of ventricular myocardium and asynchronous activation of the atrial and ventricular chambers. Biventricular pacing attempts to activate the right and left ventricles simultaneously, producing what is termed “ventricular resynchronization”. [0007] Studies have confirmed acute and short-term hemodynamic benefits of biventricular pacing. In addition, studies have documented improvement in the functional status of patients with CHF. Larger, prospective studies investigating the beneficial effects of biventricular pacing and its clinical implications are currently underway. [0008] In addition to the symptomatic and functional improvements, other important changes have been noted in CHF patients treated with biventricular pacing. Parameters of cardiac function such as left ventricular dimensions and myocardial performance index have improved markedly. Elevated plasma norepinephrine levels, which are associated with increased mortality in CHF, improve in biventricular pacing. Decreased heart rate variability, also associated with increased risk of sudden death in CHF, has been shown to improve. These findings have lead investigators to hypothesize the potential for biventricular pacing to improve survival. This being said, no trial to date has demonstrated a survival benefit to biventricular pacing. Furthermore, no studies are known that investigate the effects, and potential benefits, of biventricular pacing forcing a small delay between right ventricular and left ventricular contraction, or vice versa. [0009] Optimization Techniques [0010] When optimizing the AV delay, or any other delay such as a delay between the contraction of right and left ventricles, it must be tailored to the individual patient. For almost two decades, stroke volume measurements by means of thoracic electrical bioimpedance (TEB) have been favorably considered for optimal determination of pacemaker settings. More recently, Hayes et al. (Hayes D, Hayes S, Hyberger L. Atrioventricular interval optimization technique: Impedance measurements vs Echo/Doppler. Presented at the North American Society for Pacing & Electrophysiology's 19th Annual Scientific Sessions, San Diego, Calif., May 9, 1998) reported that the noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring with TEB permits determination of optimal AV delay within 15 minutes in any clinical settings. [0011] Despite promising benefits to the patient, the utilization of thoracic electrical bioimpedance (TEB), as with any other aforementioned method, has not been established as a standard optimization procedure for the setting of parameter values of dual-chamber pacemakers. Apparently, the TEB procedure, applied during pacemaker follow-up, is time-consuming and requires active involvement of the physician during the entire optimization period. [0012] Rate-responsive cardiac pacemakers address the adaptation of the pacing rate according to the physiological demands related to the activity of the pacemaker patient. Sensors determine, for example, posture and movement of the patient, or respiration, characterized by respiration rate and tidal volume, and even stroke volume by measurement of thoracic electrical bioimpedance. The pacemaker adapts the pacing rate depending on the information obtained by the sensors and processed usually by the pacemaker. The pacemaker's rate adapted to the patient's activity is not within the scope of the aforementioned optimization techniques, and the invention. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [0013] The new method and apparatus defined in the appended claims incorporate a cardiac pacemaker and thoracic electrical bioimpedance (TEB) measuring approach. With this combination of a diagnostic (TEB) and therapeutic method and apparatus (pacemaker) a closed-loop system is created to obtain, within its confines, an optimal setting of pacing parameter values. [0014] In a preferred embodiment, a specific optimization cycle, triggered by an operator or upon the expiration of a preset time interval, automatically permutates the values of one or more pacing parameters, such as AV delays, inter-atrial delay, inter-ventricular delay, or heart rate, within operator-defined ranges, and determines at each permutation of parameter values hemodynamic parameters, such as stroke volume (SV), cardiac output (CO), ejection fraction (EF), and other indices of ventricular performance. [0015] The operator defines one or more pacing parameters, such as atrioventricular delays, inter-atrial delay, inter-ventricular delay, or heart rate, which are subject to variation during an optimization cycle. DISCUSSION OF THE STATE OF THE ART [0002] Biventricular Pacing Devices [0003] Biventricular pacing devices have become increasingly prevalent for therapeutic intervention in patients showing symptoms of ventricular dysynchrony, including those with significant cardiac arrhythmias and heart failure. The benefits of such systems have been noted to include increased cardiac efficiency and potential reduction in adverse cardiac events. Nevertheless, routine fine-tuning of interventricular delay settings remains a challenge, with the majority of devices operating on factory default settings, largely due to the complex and resource-heavy nature of individualized adjustment (Jakobs K, Shivkumar K, Zebede J, et al. Individualized therapy for heart failure patients with multisite pacing devices. J Card Fail 2002; 8: 121-128). [0004] Various methods have been suggested to individualize cardiac pacing in order to maximize therapeutic outcomes, which may include echocardiographic techniques that are traditionally operator-dependent, burdensome, and costly. There exists a consensus that a broader system that facilitates routine, accessible optimization processes has yet to be established for clinical use. [0005] Recent advancements in cardiac therapy devices offer multisite pacing capabilities with potential therapeutic benefits in treating heart failure. Recognition of the importance of synchronized contraction across the cardiac chambers has led to a focus on not only atrioventricular pacing but also inter-interventricular synchronization. Reports highlight short-term physiological benefits using such strategies, but comprehensive studies proving long-term survival benefits are yet to be produced. [0006] New Techniques for Device Optimization [0007] To optimize device settings, such as interventricular and atrioventricular timing, the assessment must be highly personalized due to the significant variation in patients' cardiac profiles and the impact of concurrent medications. While echocardiography has traditionally been employed, this technique demands skilled operators and significant time, with the added limitation of being costly. Thus, there is a need for a standard optimization method that is efficient and less burdensome in clinical settings. [0008] Approaches to rate-adaptation in modern cardiac devices have seen the incorporation of sensor technologies that monitor physiological markers like respiration rate and patient activity. However, these systems are separate from the optimization of timing delays and largely function to adjust pacing rates dynamically in real time. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [0009] The invention in its embodiments describes a system that includes a multisite cardiac stimulator combined with sensing modalities for cardiac functional assessment. Creating a feedback loop within the device ecosystem, it can autonomously optimize the pacing timings based on a predefined algorithm. [0010] In a primary embodiment, the system commences an optimization sequence either manually initiated or set to a predetermined duration, that adjusts the values of pacing parameters, including interventricular and atrioventricular delay timings. The system records physiological responses, like stroke volume and ventricular performance indices, to each setting variation. [0011] The device operator sets pacing parameters, determining the range and step width for each, thus controlling the optimization's scope. The number of parameters and variation steps inform the permutation of values to be tested within the cycle. Each setting adjustment is maintained for a short, predefined period, with the intent to ascertain which configuration yields the optimal physiological response. [0012] The system utilizes current diagnostic methodologies, such as those outlined in a previously filed patent application, to measure hemodynamic parameters like stroke volume and cardiac output non-invasively. [0013] The optimization sequence, by automating the adjustment and measurement processes, offers the potential for substantial improvements in clinical efficiency when optimizing device settings during initial analysis, post-operative follow-ups, or throughout treatment for conditions such as congestive heart failure. DISCUSSION OF PRIOR ART [0002] Hybrid Power Systems [0003] Hybrid power systems in vehicles have gained prominence for their ability to improve fuel efficiency and reduce emissions. The benefits of these systems include the maximization of fuel utilization, reduction of greenhouse gases, and the provision of an auxiliary power source during engine off-cycles. However, despite the benefits of efficient power management, hybrid systems often operate on predetermined protocols which may not be optimal for every driving condition. Advanced sensors can enhance the efficiency of such systems, yet no widespread standard for sensor-driven power optimization exists. [0004] Harmonizing power flow in conjunction with sensor inputs can yield significant efficiency improvements in some vehicles with a hybrid power train, by addressing power distribution during various engine phases. Despite the potential of sensor-based optimization of power control mechanisms, such systems are commonly calibrated to OEM specifications, which might not always align with real-world driving scenarios. Current research does highlight the need for adaptive power management systems but fails to establish a universally accepted methodology. [0006] Another area of interest within the automotive industry is the development of all-electric vehicles (EVs) that utilize battery packs for propulsion. The management of battery performance and longevity is a critical aspect of EV operation. Although attempts have been made to integrate advanced battery management systems, the efficacy of such strategies in real-world conditions has yet to be affirmed through comprehensive studies. [0009] Optimization Techniques [0010] When optimizing power distribution or engine performance parameters, the approach needs to be tailored to the specific vehicle and its usage patterns. For years, real-time vehicle data monitoring has been suggested as a potential solution, yet implementing such systems has proven to be complex. Techniques such as utilizing vehicle telematics for predictive maintenance and adaptive control strategies are promising, yet their adoption across the industry remains sporadic. [0011] Despite the promise shown by these advanced systems, their application as a standard procedure for optimizing hybrid or electric vehicle performance has not been established. The complexity and the need for constant calibration based on sensor feedback have made their widespread utilization challenging. [0012] Rate-responsive automotive systems have been introduced to address the dynamic needs of power distribution based on driving conditions. Such systems use a variety of sensors to detect, for example, acceleration, vehicle inclination, or driving patterns, adjusting the power distribution as necessary. While these innovations mark progress in the field, they fall outside the scope of conventional power system optimization, distinctly separate from the topic at hand. [0016] Vehicle performance measurements are performed utilizing advanced diagnostics as detailed in a concurrent automotive patent application by the applicant. [0017] Through an automatic and systematic approach, the novel method significantly streamlines the optimization process, making it less cumbersome and more time-efficient than traditional techniques. Mechanism of hemodynamic improvement by dual-chamber pacing for severe left ventricular dysfunction: An acute Doppler and catheterization hemodynamic study. J Am Coil Cardiol 1995; 25:281-288). Despite the benefit of optimization of atrioventricular (AV) delay, dual-chamber pacemakers often are left at the default value, which the manufacturer sets to approximately 170 milliseconds (Kindermann M, Frohlig G, Doerr T, Schieffer H. Optimizing the AV delay in DDD pacemakers with high degree AVE block: Mitral valve Doppler versus impedance cardiography. Pacing Clin Electrophysiol 1997; 20: 2453-2462). It is the consensus of independent researchers that optimization of AV interval is not routinely performed. Procedures for pacemaker optimization, specifically obtaining stroke volume measurements at different AV intervals by aortic Doppler echocardiography , traditionally have been observer-dependent, time-consuming, and costly. [0005] The goal of AV optimization is the synchronization of the completion of end-diastolic filling exactly at the onset of left ventricular contraction. Obviously, to accomplish this objective, precise physiological measurements of the events of the cardiac cycle must be obtained. Because of a wide range of cardiac conditions, status of the ventricles, and cardioactive medications, each and every patient is unique. Leonelli et al. (Leonelli F, Wang K, Youssef M, Brown D. Systolic and diastolic effects of variable atrioventricular delay in patients with pacemakers. Eur Heart J 1995; 15:1431-1440) observed that an optimal setting of the AV delay value improved stroke volume up to 42%. [0006] Another application of cardiac pacemakers has recently been discovered: Recent reports are suggesting that biventricular pacing may offer some important options in the treatment of patients with congestive heart failure (CHF). A significant percentage of patients with CHF have conduction abnormalities on EGG. These conduction abnormalities result in abnormal activation of ventricular myocardium and asynchronous activation of the atrial and ventricular chambers. Biventricular pacing attempts to activate the right and left ventricles simultaneously, producing what is termed “ventricular resynchronization”. [0007] Studies have confirmed acute and short-term hemodynamic benefits of biventricular pacing. In addition, studies have documented improvement in the functional status of patients with CHF. Larger, prospective studies investigating the beneficial effects of biventricular pacing and its clinical implications are currently underway. [0008] In addition to the symptomatic and functional improvements, other important changes have been noted in CHF patients treated with biventricular pacing. Parameters of cardiac function such as left ventricular dimensions and myocardial performance index have improved markedly. Elevated plasma norepinephrine levels, which are associated with increased mortality in CHF, improve in biventricular pacing. Decreased heart rate variability, also associated with increased risk of sudden death in CHF, has been shown to improve. These findings have lead investigators to hypothesize the potential for biventricular pacing to improve survival. This being said, no trial to date has demonstrated a survival benefit to biventricular pacing. Furthermore, no studies are known that investigate the effects, and potential benefits, of biventricular pacing forcing a small delay between right ventricular and left ventricular contraction, or vice versa. [0009] Optimization Techniques [0010] When optimizing the AV delay, or any other delay such as a delay between the contraction of right and left ventricles, it must be tailored to the individual patient. For almost two decades, stroke volume measurements by means of thoracic electrical bioimpedance (TEB) have been favorably considered for optimal determination of pacemaker settings. More recently, Hayes et al. (Hayes D, Hayes S, Hyberger L. Atrioventricular interval optimization technique: Impedance measurements vs Echo/Doppler. Presented at the North American Society for Pacing & Electrophysiology's 19th Annual Scientific Sessions, San Diego, Calif., May 9, 1998) reported that the noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring with TEB permits determination of optimal AV delay within 15 minutes in any clinical settings. [0011] Despite promising benefits to the patient, the utilization of thoracic electrical bioimpedance (TEB), as with any other aforementioned method, has not been established as a standard optimization procedure for the setting of parameter values of dual-chamber pacemakers. Apparently, the TEB procedure, applied during pacemaker follow-up, is time-consuming and requires active involvement of the physician during the entire optimization period. [0012] Rate-responsive cardiac pacemakers address the adaptation of the pacing rate according to the physiological demands related to the activity of the pacemaker patient. Sensors determine, for example, posture and movement of the patient, or respiration, characterized by respiration rate and tidal volume, and even stroke volume by measurement of thoracic electrical bioimpedance. positive: FIELD OF INVENTION [0001] The invention pertains to advancements in vehicular power systems, in particular to a method that harmonizes power distribution with engine performance optimization. DISCUSSION OF PRIOR ART [0002] Hybrid Power Systems [0003] Hybrid power systems in vehicles have gained prominence for their ability to improve fuel efficiency and reduce emissions. The benefits of these systems include the maximization of fuel utilization, reduction of greenhouse gases, and the provision of an auxiliary power source during engine off-cycles. However, despite the benefits of efficient power management, hybrid systems often operate on predetermined protocols which may not be optimal for every driving condition. Advanced sensors can enhance the efficiency of such systems, yet no widespread standard for sensor-driven power optimization exists. [0004] Harmonizing power flow in conjunction with sensor inputs can yield significant efficiency improvements in some vehicles with a hybrid power train, by addressing power distribution during various engine phases. Despite the potential of sensor-based optimization of power control mechanisms, such systems are commonly calibrated to OEM specifications, which might not always align with real-world driving scenarios. Current research does highlight the need for adaptive power management systems but fails to establish a universally accepted methodology. [0006] Another area of interest within the automotive industry is the development of all-electric vehicles (EVs) that utilize battery packs for propulsion. The management of battery performance and longevity is a critical aspect of EV operation. Although attempts have been made to integrate advanced battery management systems, the efficacy of such strategies in real-world conditions has yet to be affirmed through comprehensive studies. [0009] Optimization Techniques [0010] When optimizing power distribution or engine performance parameters, the approach needs to be tailored to the specific vehicle and its usage patterns. For years, real-time vehicle data monitoring has been suggested as a potential solution, yet implementing such systems has proven to be complex. Techniques such as utilizing vehicle telematics for predictive maintenance and adaptive control strategies are promising, yet their adoption across the industry remains sporadic. [0011] Despite the promise shown by these advanced systems, their application as a standard procedure for optimizing hybrid or electric vehicle performance has not been established. The complexity and the need for constant calibration based on sensor feedback have made their widespread utilization challenging. [0012] Rate-responsive automotive systems have been introduced to address the dynamic needs of power distribution based on driving conditions. Such systems use a variety of sensors to detect, for example, acceleration, vehicle inclination, or driving patterns, adjusting the power distribution as necessary. While these innovations mark progress in the field, they fall outside the scope of conventional power system optimization, distinctly separate from the topic at hand. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [0013] The novel method and apparatus outlined herein detail an integrated vehicle power system that combines sensor input with advanced algorithms to create a closed-loop system for optimal engine performance. [0014] In a preferred embodiment, the system automatically assesses various power system parameters, such as battery charge state, alternator output, and energy recovery efficiency, and adjusts these parameters as necessary to maximize vehicle performance. [0015] The defined optimization process, initiated either by an operator or automatically at set intervals, systematically tests and records data pertaining to various powertrain parameters. [0016] Vehicle performance measurements are performed utilizing advanced diagnostics as detailed in a concurrent automotive patent application by the applicant. [0017] Through an automatic and systematic approach, the novel method significantly streamlines the optimization process, making it less cumbersome and more time-efficient than traditional techniques. [0018] Other advantages, features, and objectives of the invention will become apparent from the following descriptions. [0020] [0020]FIG. 2 depicts a separate power management module interfacing with a vehicle's engine control unit (ECU). [0021] [0021]FIG. 3 outlines the steps involved in the power system optimization process.
negative: FIELD OF INVENTION [0001] The invention pertains broadly to the management of cardiovascular health, specifically to advancements in electromechanical devices designed to correct cardiac dysrhythmias. BRIEF REVIEW OF RELEVANT TECHNOLOGIES [0002] Single-Chamber Pacemakers [0003] Employed frequently for individuals with various forms of atrioventricular blocks and symptomatic bradyarrhythmias, single-chamber pacemakers have been known to contribute to the improvement of cardiac output by facilitating consistent ventricular contractions. However, the adjustment of device settings, such as pacing intervals, typically remains unchanged from manufacturer presets, contributing to less than optimal therapeutic outcomes. [0004] Although single-chamber device implantations are noted for their simplicity and lower cost compared to more complex systems, their inability to synchronize atrial and ventricular contractions can be disadvantageous for patients needing more precise cardiac cycle management. [0005] The challenge remains to identify a universally effective optimization protocol for personalizing pacing parameters, without incurring prohibitive costs or unduly burdening medical practitioners with complex procedures. Discussions in the field continue regarding the best practices for individualizing treatment to enhance cardiac function and prevent arrhythmogenic complications. [0006] Despite the growing consensus on the need for personalized care, the industry has not yet standardized an approach to modifying pacing parameters in response to patient-specific cardiac conditions. Furthermore, the direct impact of such optimizations on clinical outcomes, particularly in the context of single-chamber pacemakers, remains inadequately explored. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [0013] The proposed method and apparatus do not claim to introduce the use of thoracic electrical bioimpedance (TEB) measurements in conjunction with pacing devices. Instead, the innovation focuses on creating a semi-automated framework aimed at facilitating the adjustment of pacing parameters while considering individual patient characteristics. [0014] The preferred embodiment involves a semi-automated cycle that is initiated by a clinician or after a pre-set duration. It systematically alters the settings of various pacing parameters in a pre-defined range, recording cardiac performance indicators such as stroke volume and ejection fraction at each setting. [0015] The clinician sets the parameters to be varied, like pacing intervals, alongside the range of these variations, and the methodical steps to iterate through this range. The system tests each iterated configuration for a specified period, analyzes the collected data, and thereafter, suggests the optimal setting for the device to employ. [0016] Though the semi-automated cycle simplifies the clinician's tasks in pacing optimization and streamlines patient data collection, it stops short of creating a fully integrated, autonomous closed-loop system. FIELD OF INVENTION [0002] The present invention generally relates to a system and a method to deliver percutaneous stimulation to relieve pain and improve function in patients with back pain. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION [0003] Back pain (e.g., low back pain (LBP) lasting approximately 12 weeks) affects approximately tens of millions of people in the U.S. and is the second leading cause of disability (6.8 million people). Back pain is associated with reduced activities of daily living (e.g., walking, housework, personal care) and health-related quality of life. In addition, back pain is expensive to treat and often leads to missed work days (149 million days/year) and reduced productivity, resulting in total costs of $100-200 billion/year in the U.S. [0004] Present methods to relieve back pain are ineffective, expensive, inconvenient, and/or invasive. For example, oral medications (e.g., acetaminophen, NSAIDs, muscle relaxants, tricyclic antidepressants, antiepileptics, and corticosteroids) provide only limited and/or short-lived pain relief, and typically produce side effects (e.g., sedation, dizziness, and gastrointestinal problems). Although opioids can provide substantial short-term pain relief, they are not recommended as a treatment to control chronic back pain, since long-term use can result in dependence and severe side effects. [0005] Exercise (including yoga, stretching, strength training) has a low level of risk and can relieve pain and improve function long-term, but patients often fail to comply with treatment regimens due to discomfort, lack of motivation, and inconvenience. [0006] Physical manipulation (i.e., massage, spinal manipulation) has a low level of risk and can provide short-term pain relief. However, evidence for the long-term benefit of physical manipulation has been mixed. Further, frequent treatment sessions are required to maintain pain relief, which is inconvenient for patients. [0007] Acupuncture is minimally-invasive, and studies have suggested that acupuncture can provide pain relief. However, study design in acupuncture studies has been questionable (e.g., adequacy of sham/placebo/control), and the effectiveness of acupuncture remains controversial. [0008] Injections of steroids or anesthetic provide short-term pain relief but seldom produce long-term benefit. As well, injections of such medicines produce side effects, including increased pain, lightheadedness, headache, infection, and nausea and vomiting. [0009] Intrathecal drug therapy can be effective for reducing pain but requires an invasive procedure and is limited by a host of frequent side effects (e.g., nausea, infection, intrathecal granuloma). Also, technical complications (i.e., problems with catheter or pump) are common and may require reoperation or removal of the device. [0010] Surgical procedures for back pain (e.g., spinal fusion, disc replacement) are highly invasive, irreversible, carry risks of complications, and reduce pain in less than half of patients. Also, surgeries for chronic back pain frequently require reoperation. [0011] Existing methods of electrical stimulation reduce pain by generating paresthesias (i.e., tingling sensation) overlapping the regions of pain. Pain relief using these existing methods persists only for a short time following treatment (e.g., hours to days), and this suggests that chronic pain has not been reversed. As a result, only a small percentage of patients using existing methods of electrical stimulation experienced clinically significant reductions in chronic axial low back pain post-treatment. [0012] TENS is a non-invasive method to deliver electrical stimulation through surface electrodes to generate paresthesia coverage of the regions of pain. TENS requires frequent treatment sessions to maintain pain relief, but consistent efficacy in chronic low back pain has not been demonstrated. Although TENS can be self-administered at home, TENS systems are cumbersome and not practical for daily use. Also, TENS can activate cutaneous fibers and cause irritation and discomfort, limiting the maximum tolerable stimulation intensity and treatment duration that can be delivered and reducing the potential efficacy of the treatment. [0013] Spinal cord stimulation is a method to deliver electrical stimulation through implanted leads connected to an implanted pulse generator to generate paresthesia coverage of the regions of pain. Spinal cord stimulation requires complex and invasive surgery to implant the leads and pulse generator. Spinal cord stimulation has a moderate rate of complications, including additional pain and hardware complications, and as a result, revision surgery, reprogramming, or removal of the stimulator is often required. [0014] In summary, present treatments for back pain seldom provide adequate long-term relief of pain or improvements in function; carry risks of side effects and complications; and/or are invasive. [0015] There remains room in the art of pain management for unproved systems and methods to be used to assist in the treatment of back pain. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [0016] Embodiments according to the present invention provide improved systems and methods to be used to assist in the treatment of back pain. [0017] The invention provides an electrical stimulation device having at least one electrode adapted for insertion within an animal body with back pain and at least one pulse generator operatively coupled with the at least one electrode, wherein the pulse generator delivers electrical stimulation activating at least one muscle in a back of the animal body for pain relief. [0018] The invention also provides an electrical stimulation device having at least one electrode adapted for insertion below skin of an animal body with back pain and a pulse generator operatively coupled with the at least one electrode, wherein the pulse generator delivers electrical stimulation for a prescribed period of time to activate at least one muscle in a back of the animal body to relive pain. [0019] The invention further provides a method to alleviate back pain including placing at least one electrode within a tissue of an animal body, and applying stimulation through the at least one electrode to activate at least one muscle in a back of the animal body with back pain. Alternatively, the pulse generator may transmit signals without a physical connection to the electrode (e.g., radio-frequency coupling, passive polarization of electrode) or may be housed within a single unit along with the electrode.
